steps.title: How does Google decide who to show?
steps.text: Think of Google as a giant librarian. To recommend your website it has to do three things, and at each step you can win or lose customers.

items.title: It finds your website
items.text: Google explores the web by following links. If your website is slow, riddled with errors or poorly linked, some pages simply never get seen.
items.work: **What I work on:** speed, sitemap, internal links, technical errors.

items.title: It works out what you do
items.text: It reads titles, copy and structured data to understand what you offer, to whom and where. Send mixed messages and you’ll show up for the wrong searches.
items.work: **What I work on:** keywords, content, page structure.

items.title: It picks who gets the top spot
items.text: Out of every website answering the same question, it rewards the most useful, trustworthy and enjoyable to use.
items.work: **What I work on:** authority, reviews, user experience.

ai.title: More and more people ask AI. Will it mention you?
ai.text: ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Google’s AI Overviews reply in plain text and cite only a handful of sources. I work to make your website one of them, with clear, verifiable information that’s easy to summarize. It’s called **GEO** (Generative Engine Optimization), and it stands on the same foundations as good SEO.

items.question: How soon will I see results?
items.answer: Once technical issues are fixed, early signs often appear within a few weeks. Solid results for competitive searches usually take 3 to 6 months. The upside: unlike ads, they stick around.

items.question: How much does SEO consulting cost?
items.answer: It depends on the option and the size of your website. The audit has a fixed price; ongoing SEO a fixed monthly fee. It’s all in writing in the quote, after the free call.

items.question: Can you guarantee me the top spot on Google?
items.answer: No, and be wary of anyone who does: nobody controls Google’s algorithm. What I guarantee is methodical work, clear priorities and full transparency about what I do and what you get.

items.question: Do I need a new website for SEO?
items.answer: Hardly ever. Most websites can be improved a great deal without a rebuild. If yours has structural limits, I’ll tell you straight and walk you through the alternatives.

items.question: Can you work with my agency or developer?
items.answer: Yes, happily. I can do the work myself or write precise instructions for whoever already looks after your website.

items.question: Do you do SEO for websites in other languages?
items.answer: Yes: I speak English, German and Spanish and handle multilingual websites, from the technical setup to keyword research for each market.
